- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion or volatility.
- Model tends to lag in early periods of strong sentiment trends; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3–5 days of rising sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward correction if price has been above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment >0.67 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 0.67 to 0.00), model often fails to adjust; apply a 2–4% upward correction to avoid underestimating rebound.
